headline: Dry and mild through Wednesday, a weak front Thursday, then an uncertain weekend system.
summary: A large area of low pressure sliding south toward California is passing well offshore, while a ridge of high pressure to the north keeps western Washington dry. Expect dry, mild weather through Wednesday. Patchy fog may form on a few mornings, mainly in cooler valleys, with some frost in the south interior. Afternoons warm a few degrees by Wednesday, with the best chance of near 70 in the south interior. A weak cold front arrives Thursday into Friday, bringing the best chance of showers east of I-5 up to the Cascades. Highs drop into the 50s, with 30s in valleys and mountains and perhaps a few 20s. Another system may reach the region next weekend, but computer models disagree on its track, so whether it brings rain or snow is a tossup. Either way, snow levels are expected to fall to 4,000 to 5,000 feet going into the weekend.
changes: The morning discussion warned of a possible wind and rain storm Saturday into Sunday, but the later discussions dropped wind from the weekend outlook and described a system that could bring either rain or snow. Fog was also expected to be less widespread, limited mostly to cooler valleys.
